atoms.title: Operating working capital

atoms.title: Operating cash flow

atoms.title: Capital expenditure

atoms.title: Depreciation

featured_connections.why: Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.
Non-cash depreciation deducted in operating profit is added back in the standard FCFF build.
Depreciable PPE is allocated to expense over useful lives.
Fixed-asset schedules link capex, disposals and depreciation.

atoms.title: EBIT
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within EBITDA, EBIT, and operating profit
atoms.focus: Earnings before interest and tax; specify adjustments and reconcile it with reported operating profit.
atoms.hook: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?

Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.

atoms.title: NOPAT
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
atoms.focus: After-tax operating profit for the specified operating perimeter; a simplified model uses EBIT multiplied by one minus an operating tax rate.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: NOPAT is a starting point for FCFF before non-cash adjustments and reinvestment.
Operating earnings provide the profit base for after-tax operating profit.
Tax depreciation affects operating cash taxes separately from book depreciation.

atoms.title: Free cash flow to the firm (FCFF)
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
atoms.focus: Cash available to all capital providers after operating taxes and reinvestment, before financing distributions.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: FCFF is discounted at a matching WACC in a standard enterprise DCF.
An enterprise DCF discounts future FCFF and a consistent terminal value.
Non-cash depreciation deducted in operating profit is added back in the standard FCFF build.
Cash operating capital expenditure is deducted when calculating standard FCFF.

atoms.title: Free cash flow to equity (FCFE)
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
atoms.focus: Cash available to equity after reinvestment, debt cash flows and other relevant financing claims.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: FCFE is discounted at a matching cost of equity.
An equity DCF discounts future FCFE and an equity-consistent terminal value.
Net borrowing is included in a conventional FCFE reconciliation.
LBO equity outcomes depend on cash available after debt service and exit claims.

atoms.title: Weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Weighted average cost of capital
atoms.focus: Market-value-weighted required return on the financing mix, with applicable debt tax treatment.
atoms.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

featured_connections.why: FCFF is discounted at a matching WACC in a standard enterprise DCF.
ROIC above a comparable cost of capital is a value-creation diagnostic.
Usable debt interest deductions affect conventional after-tax WACC.
Debt required return and applicable tax treatment enter WACC.

atoms.title: Cost of equity
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Cost of equity
atoms.focus: Required return of equity investors for the risk of the equity claim.
atoms.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

featured_connections.why: FCFE is discounted at a matching cost of equity.

atoms.title: Enterprise value
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Enterprise value versus equity value
atoms.focus: Value of the specified operating enterprise available to its capital providers; reconcile the perimeter to equity value.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: The enterprise-to-equity bridge reconciles operating value to shareholder value.
Discounted operating FCFF estimates the specified operating enterprise value.

atoms.title: Equity value
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Enterprise value versus equity value
atoms.focus: Value attributable to common equity after the relevant non-equity claims and non-operating adjustments.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: The bridge adds relevant non-operating assets and removes non-equity claims.

atoms.title: Expected credit losses
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Expected credit losses
atoms.focus: Probability-weighted credit-loss estimates under the applicable impairment framework.
atoms.hook: Could this borrower repay under a plausible downside scenario?

featured_connections.why: Credit-loss expense can reduce reported profit without a contemporaneous cash payment.
Uncollected customer balances may require an expected credit-loss allowance.
Default likelihood, loss severity and exposure inform credit-loss estimation.

atoms.title: Net borrowing
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Debt issuance and repayment
atoms.focus: Cash proceeds from new debt less cash principal repayments over the specified period.
atoms.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

featured_connections.why: Net borrowing is included in a conventional FCFE reconciliation.
Financing debt proceeds and principal repayments do not form operating FCFF.
Debt schedules forecast debt drawdowns, repayments and interest.

atoms.title: Discounted cash flow (DCF)
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within Discounted cash-flow valuation
atoms.focus: Value expected future cash flows by discounting at a rate matched to their risk, currency and investor claim.
atoms.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: Discounted operating FCFF estimates the specified operating enterprise value.
An enterprise DCF discounts future FCFF and a consistent terminal value.
An equity DCF discounts future FCFE and an equity-consistent terminal value.

atoms.title: Return on invested capital (ROIC)
atoms.original: Added atomic anchor within ROA, ROE, ROCE, and ROIC
atoms.focus: After-tax operating profit relative to the invested capital used to generate it, using consistent timing and scope.
atoms.hook: Could this ratio improve while the underlying business becomes weaker?

featured_connections.why: ROIC above a comparable cost of capital is a value-creation diagnostic.
Reinvestment and incremental operating returns connect growth to value creation.
Capital allocation can be assessed through operating returns and value created.

nodes.focus: Operating current assets less operating current liabilities, using an explicit definition that usually excludes cash and financing debt.
nodes.hook: Can a growing business run out of cash before customers pay?

featured_connections.why: Increases in operating working capital generally reduce operating cash flow in the indirect reconciliation.
An increase in operating working capital is deducted in the standard FCFF build.
Operating receivables are one component of operating working capital.
Operating inventory is included in operating working capital.

nodes.title: Operating cash flow
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Cash flow from operations, investing, and financing
nodes.focus: Cash generated or used by operating activities, classified under the applicable reporting framework.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

featured_connections.why: Increases in operating working capital generally reduce operating cash flow in the indirect reconciliation.

nodes.title: Capital expenditure
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Capital expenditure and asset disposal proceeds
nodes.focus: Cash invested in qualifying long-lived operating assets; it is distinct from the period depreciation expense.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

featured_connections.why: Cash operating capital expenditure is deducted when calculating standard FCFF.
Capital expenditure is distinguished from current operating expense.
Telecom and digital infrastructure require capital-intensity and reinvestment analysis.

nodes.title: Depreciation
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Depreciation, amortisation, and impairment
nodes.focus: Allocation of a depreciable asset cost over its useful life; generally a non-cash expense in the period.
nodes.hook: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?

featured_connections.why: Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.
Non-cash depreciation deducted in operating profit is added back in the standard FCFF build.
Depreciable PPE is allocated to expense over useful lives.
Fixed-asset schedules link capex, disposals and depreciation.

nodes.title: EBIT
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within EBITDA, EBIT, and operating profit
nodes.focus: Earnings before interest and tax; specify adjustments and reconcile it with reported operating profit.
nodes.hook: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?

featured_connections.why: Operating earnings provide the profit base for after-tax operating profit.
Depreciation reduces EBIT for depreciating operating assets.

nodes.title: NOPAT
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
nodes.focus: After-tax operating profit for the specified operating perimeter; a simplified model uses EBIT multiplied by one minus an operating tax rate.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: NOPAT is a starting point for FCFF before non-cash adjustments and reinvestment.
Operating earnings provide the profit base for after-tax operating profit.
Tax depreciation affects operating cash taxes separately from book depreciation.

nodes.title: Free cash flow to the firm (FCFF)
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
nodes.focus: Cash available to all capital providers after operating taxes and reinvestment, before financing distributions.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: FCFF is discounted at a matching WACC in a standard enterprise DCF.
An enterprise DCF discounts future FCFF and a consistent terminal value.
Non-cash depreciation deducted in operating profit is added back in the standard FCFF build.
Cash operating capital expenditure is deducted when calculating standard FCFF.

nodes.title: Free cash flow to equity (FCFE)
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within FCFF and FCFE
nodes.focus: Cash available to equity after reinvestment, debt cash flows and other relevant financing claims.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: FCFE is discounted at a matching cost of equity.
An equity DCF discounts future FCFE and an equity-consistent terminal value.
Net borrowing is included in a conventional FCFE reconciliation.
LBO equity outcomes depend on cash available after debt service and exit claims.

nodes.title: Weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Weighted average cost of capital
nodes.focus: Market-value-weighted required return on the financing mix, with applicable debt tax treatment.
nodes.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

featured_connections.why: FCFF is discounted at a matching WACC in a standard enterprise DCF.
ROIC above a comparable cost of capital is a value-creation diagnostic.
Usable debt interest deductions affect conventional after-tax WACC.
Debt required return and applicable tax treatment enter WACC.

nodes.title: Cost of equity
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Cost of equity
nodes.focus: Required return of equity investors for the risk of the equity claim.
nodes.hook: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?

featured_connections.why: FCFE is discounted at a matching cost of equity.

nodes.title: Enterprise value
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Enterprise value versus equity value
nodes.focus: Value of the specified operating enterprise available to its capital providers; reconcile the perimeter to equity value.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: The enterprise-to-equity bridge reconciles operating value to shareholder value.
Discounted operating FCFF estimates the specified operating enterprise value.

nodes.title: Equity value
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Enterprise value versus equity value
nodes.focus: Value attributable to common equity after the relevant non-equity claims and non-operating adjustments.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: The bridge adds relevant non-operating assets and removes non-equity claims.

nodes.title: Expected credit losses
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Expected credit losses
nodes.focus: Probability-weighted credit-loss estimates under the applicable impairment framework.
nodes.hook: Could this borrower repay under a plausible downside scenario?

featured_connections.why: Credit-loss expense can reduce reported profit without a contemporaneous cash payment.
Uncollected customer balances may require an expected credit-loss allowance.
Default likelihood, loss severity and exposure inform credit-loss estimation.

nodes.title: Net borrowing
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Debt issuance and repayment
nodes.focus: Cash proceeds from new debt less cash principal repayments over the specified period.
nodes.hook: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?

featured_connections.why: Net borrowing is included in a conventional FCFE reconciliation.
Financing debt proceeds and principal repayments do not form operating FCFF.
Debt schedules forecast debt drawdowns, repayments and interest.

nodes.title: Discounted cash flow (DCF)
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within Discounted cash-flow valuation
nodes.focus: Value expected future cash flows by discounting at a rate matched to their risk, currency and investor claim.
nodes.hook: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?

featured_connections.why: Discounted operating FCFF estimates the specified operating enterprise value.
An enterprise DCF discounts future FCFF and a consistent terminal value.
An equity DCF discounts future FCFE and an equity-consistent terminal value.

nodes.title: Return on invested capital (ROIC)
nodes.original: Added atomic anchor within ROA, ROE, ROCE, and ROIC
nodes.focus: After-tax operating profit relative to the invested capital used to generate it, using consistent timing and scope.
nodes.hook: Could this ratio improve while the underlying business becomes weaker?

featured_connections.why: ROIC above a comparable cost of capital is a value-creation diagnostic.
Reinvestment and incremental operating returns connect growth to value creation.
Capital allocation can be assessed through operating returns and value created.

purpose.1: identify who supplies capital, who uses it, and how value and risk move
purpose.2: choose the right mathematical or statistical tool and interpret its result
purpose.3: compare amounts received or paid at different times on a consistent basis
purpose.4: recognise and measure transactions before interpreting financial statements
purpose.5: trace revenue and expenses into the profit measures used in analysis
purpose.6: explain how assets are funded and how balances change through transactions
purpose.7: reconcile accounting performance with actual cash movement
purpose.8: understand recognition and measurement choices that change reported numbers
purpose.9: interpret performance using consistent denominators, periods and peer context
purpose.10: test whether reported performance is supported by cash, disclosures and controls
purpose.11: connect operating choices and customer economics to financial performance
purpose.12: compare uses of capital using incremental cash flows and risk
purpose.13: match financing risk, capital claims and required returns
purpose.14: manage the timing gap between cash receipts, payments and funding
purpose.15: translate operating assumptions into plans, decisions and explanations of variance
purpose.16: connect schedules into an internally consistent and auditable model
purpose.17: match cash flows, reinvestment, discount rates and investor claims
purpose.18: compare value using economically comparable businesses and consistent measures
purpose.19: translate business analysis into an investment thesis and understand trading mechanics
purpose.20: relate debt cash flows, yields, interest-rate sensitivity and credit quality
purpose.21: understand contingent payoffs, pricing inputs and hedge limitations
purpose.22: combine assets to meet goals and evaluate risk-adjusted performance
purpose.23: understand asset exposure, fund structures, fees, liquidity and measured performance
purpose.24: connect credit origination, bank funding, loan losses and regulatory capital
purpose.25: identify exposures, measure losses and design governance and controls
purpose.26: separate operating value, financing, deal terms and execution risk
purpose.27: connect operating milestones, cash runway, financing terms and founder ownership
purpose.28: link asset or project cash flows, debt service and investor distributions
purpose.29: connect uncertain claims, premiums, reserves, investments and solvency
purpose.30: connect household cash flow, goals, protection, investing and long-term wealth
purpose.31: distinguish accounting outcomes from tax outcomes and compare after-tax cash flows
purpose.32: trace economic conditions and policy transmission into funding, earnings and asset prices
purpose.33: keep currency exposure, cash flows, financing and discount rates consistent
purpose.34: understand how transactions are executed, safeguarded and governed
purpose.35: recognise how incentives and cognitive biases influence financial decisions
purpose.36: connect financial infrastructure, digital distribution, unit economics and controls
purpose.37: connect financing decisions with sustainability, inclusion and alternative structures
purpose.38: produce reproducible financial analysis without data leakage or model misuse
purpose.39: adapt statement interpretation, operating metrics and valuation to the industry
purpose.40: apply multiple concepts to one decision and explain the result using evidence

hooks.1: Who provides the money, who bears the risk, and who receives the benefit?
hooks.2: Could a mathematically correct answer still be financially misleading?
hooks.3: Would you prefer the money today or later, and what rate changes your answer?
hooks.4: Which accounts change when this transaction happens?
hooks.5: Can this change reported profit without changing cash today?
hooks.6: Where did this balance come from, and what transaction would change it?
hooks.7: Why might cash move differently from reported profit?
hooks.8: Would another accounting treatment change the result without changing the business?
hooks.9: Could this ratio improve while the underlying business becomes weaker?
hooks.10: What evidence would make you doubt the reported number?
hooks.11: Can selling more make the business less profitable?
hooks.12: Would this decision create value after allowing for risk and opportunity cost?
hooks.13: Which investor claim bears this risk and which return compensates for it?
hooks.14: Can a growing business run out of cash before customers pay?
hooks.15: Which operating assumption explains the gap between plan and actual results?
hooks.16: If this input changes, which schedules should change with it?
hooks.17: Does this valuation use the right cash flow for the right investor?
hooks.18: Are these businesses comparable enough for this multiple to mean anything?
hooks.19: What would have to happen for your investment thesis to be wrong?
hooks.20: Which matters more here: a change in yields, credit quality or payment timing?
hooks.21: What is the payoff if the market moves against your position?
hooks.22: Would this investment improve the portfolio rather than just look attractive alone?
hooks.23: How do fees, illiquidity and the fund structure change the investor outcome?
hooks.24: Could this borrower repay under a plausible downside scenario?
hooks.25: Which exposure is missing from the headline risk number?
hooks.26: Is the proposed value coming from the business, synergies or financing?
hooks.27: How long can this startup operate and who owns it after the next round?
hooks.28: Does this asset generate enough cash when the debt payments fall due?
hooks.29: What happens if claims arrive sooner or cost more than expected?
hooks.30: Does this choice move you closer to your goal without weakening protection?
hooks.31: What changes when you compare after-tax cash rather than accounting profit?
hooks.32: Through which channel would this policy change affect a company or portfolio?
hooks.33: What happens if the currency moves against the cash flow you expect?
hooks.34: What protects the investor between placing a trade and receiving the asset?
hooks.35: Would you make the same choice if the information were framed differently?
hooks.36: Who earns money from the transaction and who carries the credit or fraud risk?
hooks.37: How would you distinguish a measurable impact from a financing label?
hooks.38: Could information unavailable at the time be making this result look better?
hooks.39: Which metric or valuation convention changes in this industry?
hooks.40: Can you explain the decision by connecting the statements, risks and valuation?
